questions.question: Q1. State the triangle law of vector addition.
questions.answer: If two vectors are represented by two sides of a triangle taken in order, the third side (head to tail) represents the resultant in magnitude and direction.
questions.shortcut: Draw a→b head-to-tail; the closing side = a+b.
questions.example: Walking 3 m N then 4 m E → resultant 5 m NE (3-4-5 triangle).

questions.question: Q2. State the parallelogram law of vector addition.
questions.answer: If two vectors acting at a point are the adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the diagonal from that point is the resultant. R = √(A²+B²+2ABcosθ), direction tanα = Bsinθ/(A+Bcosθ).
questions.shortcut: R² = A² + B² + 2ABcosθ; θ is the angle between them.
questions.example: A=3,B=4,θ=90° → R=5 N at 53° from A.

questions.question: Q3. State the polygon law of vectors.
questions.answer: If several vectors are represented by the sides of a polygon in order, the closing side represents the resultant; if the polygon closes, the resultant is zero.
questions.example: A+B+C+D+E=0 when they form a closed pentagon in sequence.

questions.question: Q4. Find the resultant of two equal vectors inclined at 120°.
questions.answer: R = √(A²+A²+2A²cos120°) = √(2A² − A²) = A. The resultant equals each vector and bisects the angle.
questions.example: Two 10 N forces 120° apart → 10 N resultant along the bisector.

questions.question: Q5. When is the resultant of two vectors maximum and minimum?
questions.answer: Maximum (A+B) when θ=0° (same direction). Minimum (|A−B|) when θ=180° (opposite). ▥ 2.1 Laws of Vector Addition  —  Compare / Contrast Tables The Two Laws of Vector Addition ▣ 2.2 Resolution of Vectors & Unit Vectors
questions.example: 3 N & 4 N → max 7 N, min 1 N.

questions.question: Q6. Resolve a vector A into its x and y components.
questions.answer: Aₓ = A cosθ, Aᵧ = A sinθ, where θ is measured from the positive x-axis. Then A = Aₓî + Aᵧĵ.
questions.shortcut: cos goes with the axis the angle is measured from; sin goes perpendicular.

questions.question: Q7. Define unit vectors î and ĵ and state their properties.
questions.answer: Unit vectors have magnitude 1 and point along the axes: î along x, ĵ along y. Properties: î·ĵ=0, î·î=1, î×ĵ=k̂.
questions.shortcut: Dot of perpendicular unit vectors = 0; same = 1.
questions.example: Any vector can be written A = Aₓî + Aᵧĵ using these.

questions.question: Q8. Given A = 3î + 4ĵ, find its magnitude and direction.
Q9. Explain resolution of a vector into two components along two axes.
questions.answer: Drop perpendiculars from the tip of the vector onto each axis; the intercepts give the components. Along x and y: Aₓ=Acosθ, Aᵧ=Asinθ; the original equals the vector sum of its components. ▥ 2.2 Resolution of Vectors & Unit Vectors  —  Compare / Contrast Tables Resolution of a Vector: Formula Sheet ▣ 2.3 Scalar & Vector Products
questions.shortcut: Component = projection of the vector onto the axis.
questions.example: A force 20 N at 30° to vertical → horizontal = 20sin30°=10 N, vertical = 20cos30°=17.3 N.

questions.question: Q10. Define the scalar (dot) product of two vectors.
questions.answer: A·B = ABcosθ, a scalar. It equals the product of one vector and the projection of the other onto it.
questions.shortcut: Dot product → ABcosθ; perpendicular vectors give 0.

questions.question: Q11. Define the vector (cross) product and give its magnitude and direction.
questions.answer: A×B is a vector of magnitude ABsinθ, direction perpendicular to the plane by the right-hand rule (fingers a→b, thumb gives result).
questions.shortcut: Cross → ABsinθ; parallel vectors give 0, perpendicular give max AB.
questions.example: Torque τ = r×F; at right angle τ = rF.

questions.question: Q12. If A = 2î+3ĵ and B = 4î−î, compute A·B and the angle.
questions.shortcut: Dot = Σ(xᵢxᵢ'); angle via cosθ = A·B/(|A||B|).
questions.example: Used to find angles between forces.

questions.question: Q13. Show that two vectors with A·B = 0 are perpendicular.
questions.answer: Since A·B = ABcosθ, if A·B = 0 (A,B≠0) then cosθ = 0, so θ = 90°. Hence the vectors are perpendicular. ▥ 2.3 Scalar & Vector Products  —  Compare / Contrast Tables Scalar (Dot) vs Vector (Cross) Product PROFESSOR'S THEORY & VIVA BANK   — the kinds of theory a professor / examiner actually asks

theoryItems.question: [Derive] T1. Derive the resultant of two vectors from the parallelogram law.
theoryItems.answer: Place vectors as adjacent sides; by the law of cosines on the triangle, R² = A² + B² + 2ABcosθ, and the direction angle α from the first vector satisfies tanα = Bsinθ/(A+Bcosθ).

theoryItems.question: [Derive] T2. Resolve a vector into rectangular components and find magnitude/direction.
theoryItems.answer: For A at angle θ to x: Aₓ = Acosθ, Aᵧ = Asinθ. Magnitude |A| = √(Aₓ²+Aᵧ²); direction θ = tan⁻¹(Aᵧ/Aₓ).
theoryItems.shortcut: A = Aₓî + Aᵧĵ; check both components.

theoryItems.question: [State] T3. Define a vector and a scalar; give two of each.
theoryItems.answer: Scalar: fully described by magnitude (mass, time, energy). Vector: needs magnitude AND direction (force, velocity, displacement).

theoryItems.question: [State] T4. Write the scalar and vector products of unit vectors î, ĵ, k̂.
theoryItems.answer: î·î = 1, î·ĵ = 0; î×ĵ = k̂, ĵ×k̂ = î, k̂×î = ĵ... (cyclic). These define orientation.
theoryItems.shortcut: Same→1, perpendicular→0; cross follows right-hand rule.

theoryItems.question: [Compare] T5. Compare scalar and vector products; when is each zero?
theoryItems.answer: Scalar (dot): A·B = ABcosθ, a scalar; zero when θ=90° (perpendicular). Vector (cross): A×B = ABsinθ n̂, a vector; zero when θ=0 or 180° (parallel).
theoryItems.example: Work uses dot; torque uses cross.

theoryItems.question: [Explain] T6. Explain the polygon law of vectors and use it to show a closed loop sums to zero.
theoryItems.answer: Vectors placed head-to-tail form a polygon; if the last tip meets the first, the resultant is zero. Used for the equilibrium of forces: forces in a closed polygon balance.
theoryItems.example: A body at rest under coplanar forces → force polygon closes.

theoryItems.question: [Viva] T7. A professor asks: 'Give the physical meaning of A·B and A×B.'
theoryItems.answer: A·B = projection of B on A times |A| — measures 'how much of B is along A' (work = F·s). A×B is perpendicular to both, magnitude = area of the parallelogram spanned (torque = r×F).
theoryItems.shortcut: Dot = aligned part; Cross = perpendicular/area part.

theoryItems.question: [Numerical] T8. Three forces 5 N, 8 N, 10 N act on a body and keep it in equilibrium. Find the angle between the 8 N and 10 N forces.
theoryItems.answer: Since they balance, 5 N = |8×10| resultant of the other two in opposition. R² = 8²+10²−2(8)(10)cosφ = 5² → 164 − 160cosφ = 25 → cosφ = 139/160 → φ ≈ 29°.
theoryItems.shortcut: Use |R| of the two = the third (closure).
theoryItems.example: Equilibrium means the force triangle closes.

▣ 2.1 Laws of Vector Addition
Q1. State the triangle law of vector addition.
Answer:  If two vectors are represented by two sides of a triangle taken in order, the third side (head to tail) represents the resultant in magnitude and direction.
⚡ Shortcut:  Draw a→b head-to-tail; the closing side = a+b.
Example:  Walking 3 m N then 4 m E → resultant 5 m NE (3-4-5 triangle).
Q2. State the parallelogram law of vector addition.
Answer:  If two vectors acting at a point are the adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the diagonal from that point is the resultant. R = √(A²+B²+2ABcosθ), direction tanα = Bsinθ/(A+Bcosθ).
⚡ Shortcut:  R² = A² + B² + 2ABcosθ; θ is the angle between them.
Example:  A=3,B=4,θ=90° → R=5 N at 53° from A.
Q3. State the polygon law of vectors.
Answer:  If several vectors are represented by the sides of a polygon in order, the closing side represents the resultant; if the polygon closes, the resultant is zero.
⚡ Shortcut:  Closed loop → Σ = 0.
Example:  A+B+C+D+E=0 when they form a closed pentagon in sequence.
Q4. Find the resultant of two equal vectors inclined at 120°.
Answer:  R = √(A²+A²+2A²cos120°) = √(2A² − A²) = A. The resultant equals each vector and bisects the angle.
⚡ Shortcut:  θ=120° → R = A (since cos120° = −½).
Example:  Two 10 N forces 120° apart → 10 N resultant along the bisector.
Q5. When is the resultant of two vectors maximum and minimum?
Answer:  Maximum (A+B) when θ=0° (same direction). Minimum (|A−B|) when θ=180° (opposite).
⚡ Shortcut:  θ=0 → add; θ=180 → subtract.
Example:  3 N & 4 N → max 7 N, min 1 N.

▣ 2.2 Resolution of Vectors & Unit Vectors
Q6. Resolve a vector A into its x and y components.
Answer:  Aₓ = A cosθ, Aᵧ = A sinθ, where θ is measured from the positive x-axis. Then A = Aₓî + Aᵧĵ.
⚡ Shortcut:  cos goes with the axis the angle is measured from; sin goes perpendicular.
Q7. Define unit vectors î and ĵ and state their properties.
Answer:  Unit vectors have magnitude 1 and point along the axes: î along x, ĵ along y. Properties: î·ĵ=0, î·î=1, î×ĵ=k̂.
⚡ Shortcut:  Dot of perpendicular unit vectors = 0; same = 1.
Example:  Any vector can be written A = Aₓî + Aᵧĵ using these.
Q8. Given A = 3î + 4ĵ, find its magnitude and direction.
Answer:  |A| = √(3²+4²) = 5. Direction θ = tan⁻¹(Aᵧ/Aₓ) = tan⁻¹(4/3) = 53°.
⚡ Shortcut:  Magnitude = √(sum of squares); angle = tan⁻¹(y/x).
Example:  A classic 3-4-5 vector.
Q9. Explain resolution of a vector into two components along two axes.
Answer:  Drop perpendiculars from the tip of the vector onto each axis; the intercepts give the components. Along x and y: Aₓ=Acosθ, Aᵧ=Asinθ; the original equals the vector sum of its components.
⚡ Shortcut:  Component = projection of the vector onto the axis.
Example:  A force 20 N at 30° to vertical → horizontal = 20sin30°=10 N, vertical = 20cos30°=17.3 N.
▥ 2.2 Resolution of Vectors & Unit Vectors  —  Compare / Contrast Tables
Resolution of a Vector: Formula Sheet
▣ 2.3 Scalar & Vector Products
Q10. Define the scalar (dot) product of two vectors.
Answer:  A·B = ABcosθ, a scalar. It equals the product of one vector and the projection of the other onto it.
⚡ Shortcut:  Dot product → ABcosθ; perpendicular vectors give 0.
Example:  Work = F·s = Fscosθ; gravity·horizontal displacement = 0.
Q11. Define the vector (cross) product and give its magnitude and direction.
Answer:  A×B is a vector of magnitude ABsinθ, direction perpendicular to the plane by the right-hand rule (fingers a→b, thumb gives result).
⚡ Shortcut:  Cross → ABsinθ; parallel vectors give 0, perpendicular give max AB.
Example:  Torque τ = r×F; at right angle τ = rF.
Q12. If A = 2î+3ĵ and B = 4î−î, compute A·B and the angle.
⚡ Shortcut:  Dot = Σ(xᵢxᵢ'); angle via cosθ = A·B/(|A||B|).
Example:  Used to find angles between forces.
Q13. Show that two vectors with A·B = 0 are perpendicular.
Answer:  Since A·B = ABcosθ, if A·B = 0 (A,B≠0) then cosθ = 0, so θ = 90°. Hence the vectors are perpendicular.
⚡ Shortcut:  Zero dot product ⟹ 90°.
Example:  î·ĵ = 0, so axes are perpendicular.

▹ Derive  (derivations & long answers)
[Derive] T1. Derive the resultant of two vectors from the parallelogram law.
Answer:  Place vectors as adjacent sides; by the law of cosines on the triangle, R² = A² + B² + 2ABcosθ, and the direction angle α from the first vector satisfies tanα = Bsinθ/(A+Bcosθ).
⚡ Short / exam line:  R = √(A²+B²+2ABcosθ).
Example:  θ=90° → R = √(A²+B²); θ=0 → A+B; θ=180 → |A−B|.
[Derive] T2. Resolve a vector into rectangular components and find magnitude/direction.
Answer:  For A at angle θ to x: Aₓ = Acosθ, Aᵧ = Asinθ. Magnitude |A| = √(Aₓ²+Aᵧ²); direction θ = tan⁻¹(Aᵧ/Aₓ).
⚡ Short / exam line:  A = Aₓî + Aᵧĵ; check both components.
▹ State  (definitions, laws & formulae)
[State] T3. Define a vector and a scalar; give two of each.
Answer:  Scalar: fully described by magnitude (mass, time, energy). Vector: needs magnitude AND direction (force, velocity, displacement).
⚡ Short / exam line:  Scalar = number; Vector = number + direction.
Example:  Temperature scalar; momentum vector.
[State] T4. Write the scalar and vector products of unit vectors î, ĵ, k̂.
Answer:  î·î = 1, î·ĵ = 0; î×ĵ = k̂, ĵ×k̂ = î, k̂×î = ĵ... (cyclic). These define orientation.
⚡ Short / exam line:  Same→1, perpendicular→0; cross follows right-hand rule.
Example:  Used to add/subtract vector components.
▹ Compare  (compare & contrast)
[Compare] T5. Compare scalar and vector products; when is each zero?
Answer:  Scalar (dot): A·B = ABcosθ, a scalar; zero when θ=90° (perpendicular). Vector (cross): A×B = ABsinθ n̂, a vector; zero when θ=0 or 180° (parallel).
⚡ Short / exam line:  Dot: cos, ⟂→0; Cross: sin, ∥→0.
Example:  Work uses dot; torque uses cross.
▹ Explain  (working / principle / application)
[Explain] T6. Explain the polygon law of vectors and use it to show a closed loop sums to zero.
Answer:  Vectors placed head-to-tail form a polygon; if the last tip meets the first, the resultant is zero. Used for the equilibrium of forces: forces in a closed polygon balance.
⚡ Short / exam line:  Closed head-to-tail → Σ = 0.
Example:  A body at rest under coplanar forces → force polygon closes.
▹ Viva  (viva-voce probing)
[Viva] T7. A professor asks: 'Give the physical meaning of A·B and A×B.'
Answer:  A·B = projection of B on A times |A| — measures 'how much of B is along A' (work = F·s). A×B is perpendicular to both, magnitude = area of the parallelogram spanned (torque = r×F).
⚡ Short / exam line:  Dot = aligned part; Cross = perpendicular/area part.
Example:  F·s = work; r×F = torque.
▹ Numerical  (long numericals / problems)
[Numerical] T8. Three forces 5 N, 8 N, 10 N act on a body and keep it in equilibrium. Find the angle between the 8 N and 10 N forces.
Answer:  Since they balance, 5 N = |8×10| resultant of the other two in opposition. R² = 8²+10²−2(8)(10)cosφ = 5² → 164 − 160cosφ = 25 → cosφ = 139/160 → φ ≈ 29°.
⚡ Short / exam line:  Use |R| of the two = the third (closure).
Example:  Equilibrium means the force triangle closes.
